_seed: A RECORD of Millie's own responsibilities — NOT installed by any manifest. The live copy is her responsibility store (Firestore primes/{prime}/fleet/millie/responsibilities/<id>, adopted 2026-09-27; revision 3 on 2026-10-01 — template, names and terms, the content types the tool accepts): change it there with `responsibility-manage` (on her VM, or from Prime with --agent millie), and update this record to match if you want it kept in git. Use it only to re-create a responsibility if the store is ever lost: `responsibility-manage create --file <this responsibility as its own JSON object>`.
_setup: r-weekly-exec-update runs in the project 'exec-briefing' and follows the playbook 'p-weekly-exec-update'. The deployment creates that project with resource references (context packets {kind, name, summary}) for: each designated weekly meeting (kind 'resource'; name = the meeting's exact title, which is how Google names its notes — no folder), the exec-summaries output folder, and the brand-guide doc. Deployment bindings are project resources — never memory, which consolidation prunes (BRAIN_CANON B-5). Without the project the mission says so and stops. Give the agent the notes by INVITING it to the meetings: after each occurrence Meet shares the transcript with invitees in the host's organization (an invitee outside it receives only Gemini notes, and only when the host sends notes to all guests). Never share the host's 'Google Meet' folder instead: since July 2026 Google answers a share of that root folder by starting a new one for every later meeting.

responsibilities.name: Weekly Executive Update
responsibilities.instruction: Produce this week's Weekly Executive Update to structure the 30-minute weekly executive sync. Read the designated meetings, the briefing template, the names and terms, the output folder and the brand-guide doc from this mission's PROJECT — they are its resource references (do not look them up in memory; do not use the calendar). For each designated meeting find THIS WEEK's notes BY THE MEETING'S NAME — the '- Transcript' Google Docs that Google shares with you as an invitee, created since this time last week (never the '- Recording' video, never an older week's notes) — and SAVE the full text to a working file; a meeting with nothing new this week gets one line naming the date of its newest notes while the rest proceed, and if no designated meeting has anything new, create nothing and report what you found. Then write the briefing by FOLLOWING THE TEMPLATE, section by section and in its order, thinking across the four meetings by area the way the playbook describes — every section carrying real content drawn from the transcripts, every proper name checked against the names and terms (no empty or placeholder sections). Deliver it as ONE branded Google Doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>' in the output folder, CREATED fresh (an earlier doc with today's title goes to the trash first; ids copied verbatim; its sharing left exactly as the folder grants it) and report its link plus the section headings you read back.
responsibilities.success_criteria: This week's Weekly Executive Update exists as a branded Google Doc TITLED 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date, YYYY-MM-DD>' (not the legacy 'Weekly Executive Brief', and using today's real date) in the exec-summaries output folder, and its link is reported — its sharing left exactly as the output folder grants it (never made public or link-shared). As evidence, the agent READ THE FINISHED DOCUMENT BACK and reported its section headings AND confirmed that every section of the project's briefing template is present, in the template's order, with real, non-empty body content synthesized from the transcripts — an empty-section, placeholder or copied-guidance document does NOT satisfy this. Sourced ONLY from the designated weekly meetings' notes created since this time last week (a designated meeting with nothing new is NOTED in one line with the date of its newest notes — never backfilled with an older week's notes — and does not block the rest); no non-designated meeting is used; proper names follow the project's names and terms (the product is peregrine3); and exactly ONE doc for this week exists (an earlier same-day doc was moved to the trash, not duplicated).

context.purpose: Leadership runs a 30-minute weekly executive sync and needs one reliable, skimmable briefing, built the same way every week from that week's meeting notes.
process: READ THE PROJECT (do this first): this mission runs in its project, and the project's resource references — shown in its project context — are this deployment's weekly-exec specifics: the designated source meetings (each a resource named exactly as Google names that meeting's notes — there is no folder to read), the BRIEFING TEMPLATE doc, the NAMES AND TERMS, the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder, and the brand-guide doc. Copy every id VERBATIM from there. The playbook arrives as this mission's PLAYBOOK context — it is not a document to look up. If a required resource is missing from the project, say so and stop rather than guessing, searching memory, or using the calendar.

GATHER THIS WEEK'S NOTES, each meeting BY ITS NAME, full text saved to the workspace. You are an invitee of every designated meeting, so Google shares each occurrence's transcript with you directly: a Google Doc owned by the meeting's host, named '<meeting> - YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM <zone> - Transcript'. Find it in Drive by that name — never through a folder (Google re-creates the host's 'Google Meet' folders, so a folder id goes stale) and never through the calendar. (1) Get the cutoff, this time last week — when last week's briefing was written: date -u -d '7 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ. (2) For EACH designated meeting run: drive-search --query "name contains '<the resource's meeting name>' and (name contains 'Transcript' or name contains 'Notes by Gemini') and mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.document'" --order-by "createdTime desc" --max 4 — the mimeType term keeps out the '- Recording' video, shortcuts and folders; use only rows whose name starts with the meeting's name. (3) Every row whose 'created' time is AFTER the cutoff is this week's — normally one occurrence; a transcript that landed just after last week's briefing counts too. For each such occurrence save the full text of its '- Transcript' doc (its 'Notes by Gemini' doc only if it has no transcript): docs-cat <id> --out <meeting>.txt. Full text on disk is REQUIRED so the body is written from the transcripts, not a lossy summary. (4) If no row is newer than the cutoff, the meeting has nothing new this week — it was skipped, or it met this morning and its transcript has not landed yet. Do NOT fall back to an older week (last week's briefing covered it): note '<meeting>: nothing new this week (newest notes: <date>)' and move on without searching further. Use ONLY your designated meetings; exclude every other meeting. If NO designated meeting has anything newer than the cutoff, create nothing: report each meeting with the date of its newest notes and stop — either none of them met, or their notes are not being shared with you, and the operator needs to know which.

SYNTHESIZE — READ THE TEMPLATE, then write from the SAVED files (never from a summary). First read the template in full: docs-cat <template id from the project> --out template.txt, then read template.txt — it fixes the sections, their order and what goes in each. Read the saved transcripts back. Then build a content JSON in the docs-create-branded --content format — an array of section objects such as {"type":"heading","level":2,"text":"..."}, {"type":"heading","level":3,"text":"..."}, {"type":"paragraph","text":"..."}, {"type":"bullets","items":["..."]}, {"type":"numbered","items":["..."]}, {"type":"table","headers":[...],"rows":[[...]]} (the tool accepts exactly: heading, paragraph, bullets, numbered, table, callout, divider — it refuses any other type) — that fills EVERY section of the template in its order with this week's substance: specific decisions, owners, risks, dates, numbers. Replace every [bracketed] guidance line; never copy one into the briefing. Think across the four meetings by area, not meeting by meeting (the playbook says how). Do NOT put the document title in the JSON — docs-create-branded adds it. Check every proper name and term against the project's names and terms (the product is peregrine3). An empty, placeholder or copied-guidance section is a FAILURE.

DELIVER in one step, from the JSON you built: FIRST list the OUTPUT folder — that listing is the ONLY truth about what exists there; never reuse a doc id carried over from recall or an earlier run (it may have been trashed). If the listing shows a doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>', move it to the trash (drive-delete --file <its id>) so exactly one doc remains. Then CREATE the briefing fresh with docs-create-branded --title "Weekly Executive Update - <TODAY's actual date, YYYY-MM-DD>" --content <your content json file> --brand-doc <brand-guide id from the project> --folder <output folder id from the project> — creating is the path that carries the whole structure. NEVER change the doc's sharing (no drive-share, no public or anyone-with-the-link access): it inherits the output folder's access, and its link already works for everyone who should read it. Use TODAY's real date in the title — never a meeting date or a future date; the title must read 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' (not 'Brief'). Copy every id EXACTLY from the project's resources (verbatim). Report only what you actually did — mention a trashed doc only if you ran drive-delete.

VERIFY with evidence: read the finished doc back and report (a) its section headings — every section of the template, in its order — AND, for each, that it has real non-empty body content; an empty-section doc does NOT count as done; (b) the notes you used, each with its meeting date, and every designated meeting that had nothing new this week, with the date of its newest notes; (c) the doc's link, exactly as created (its sharing unchanged). That read-back is the proof.
